subject: Defining acceptance criteria, exit gates, and test runbook for evaluation
messages:
From: Emily Tran <emily.tran@medusis.ai>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@medusis.ai>
Date: 2026-05-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP / acceptance criteria for pilot evaluation

Hi Maya (and Ben),

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed by the latency and the native prompt tooling. We’re ready to move to a 4-week evaluation but need a clear mutual action plan and a short acceptance test runbook before procurement signs off. Key asks from our side:

- Concrete pass/fail thresholds for latency and throughput (90th/95th pct).
- Expected cost per 1M tokens estimate for the proposed config.
- A concise list of functional acceptance tests (NLU accuracy on our dataset, hallucination checks, embedding similarity recall).
- A go/no-go decision date and required evidence for sign-off.

Can you share a proposed MAP with exit gates and an attachment that maps each test to an owner and timeline? We’ll need it by EOD Tuesday to keep procurement on schedule.

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Tran
Head of Platform Integrations, Medusis Health
emily.tran@medusis.ai
+1 415-555-0182

Attachment: initial-requirements.pdf (reference only)

From: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>
To: Emily Tran <emily.tran@medusis.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace Oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-19T11:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP / acceptance criteria for pilot evaluation

Emily — thanks, and great to hear the demo resonated. Draft MAP attached (MAP-draft-v2.xlsx). High-level proposal below; I’ve kept the exit gates tight to limit procurement risk.

> From: Emily Tran <emily.tran@medusis.ai>
> Can you share a proposed MAP with exit gates and an attachment that maps each test to an owner and timeline?

Proposed MAP summary (4-week evaluation):

1) Success pillars (what must be true)
  - Latency: p95 <= 350ms for 512-token prompts on dedicated instance under expected load.
  - Throughput: sustained 40 rps across burst windows without >5% tail latency inflation.
  - Functional: intent-classification F1 >= 0.88 on your labeled sample; top-3 retrieval recall >= 0.92 for embeddings use-case.
  - Safety/QA: hallucination spot-checks < 3% in random 200-response sample; no critical PII leaks in audit sampling.

2) Exit gates (must have all to sign)
  - Evidence: runbook + test artifacts uploaded to shared Drive folder (see link).
  - Smoke: 3 production-like scenarios pass the smoke harness (scripts in eval-test-cases.md).
  - Cost: projected monthly cost within 15% of the estimate in SLA-proposal.pdf.
  - Ops: tracing + KV cache behavior observed for 72 hours with no unhandled errors.

3) Acceptance tests (owner / timeline) — full matrix in attachment
  - Performance IO: Karthik (week 1–2) — p50/p95/p99 captures, stress, and steady-state runs.
  - Functional: Ben & Medusis data team (week 2) — labeled eval, confusion matrix, edge-case probe.
  - Embeddings R-Recall: Ben (week 2–3) — batch compare against ground-truth.
  - Safety & QA: Grace (continuous) — hallucination checklist + random sampling.

4) Decision path & schedule
  - Week 1: onboarding, smoke tests, baseline captures.
  - Week 2–3: formal acceptance tests and evidence collection.
  - Week 4: executive review; final decision on Day 28.

Next steps: I’ve attached MAP-draft-v2.xlsx and eval-test-cases.md. If you confirm these thresholds I’ll lock the plan and paste the mutual action timeline into HubSpot (deal MD-45678). Can we schedule a 30-min walkthrough Wednesday 10:00am PT to go over ownership and evidence artifacts?

—Maya
Maya Srinivasan
Sr. Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
maya_srinivasan@redwood.com

Attachments: MAP-draft-v2.xlsx, eval-test-cases.md

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Tran <emily.tran@medusis.ai>
Date: 2026-05-20T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP / acceptance criteria for pilot evaluation — perf notes

Quick add — saw the thresholds and wanted to call out a couple pragmatic guardrails for the acceptance runs:

- Test harness: use sequence length distribution from Medusis production logs (Ben, can you share anonymized histogram?). p95 targets must be measured under representative batch composition (mix of short/long).
- Warm-up: include a 30-minute warm-up with realistic KV cache priming before capturing final metrics.
- Stability: require 24h of stable p95 within +/-10% before calling the perf gate green — this avoids fluke passes.
- Extended smoke: add a single failover test (regional fallback) — must not increase critical error rate > 1%.

I’ll own the perf report and attach the raw captures to the Drive folder.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Performance Engineering, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: Emily Tran <emily.tran@medusis.ai>

Subject: Re: MAP / acceptance criteria for pilot evaluation — ack and next steps

Thanks, team — this is exactly the level of detail procurement needs. Quick notes and confirmations before we lock: 

- We can deliver the anonymized sequence histograms by Monday morning.
- Medusis accepts the p95 <= 350ms target as long as the stability window (24h) is enforced.
- We’d like the final decision meeting to include our Head of Product (Rajiv) — I’ve cc’d him on the original thread.
- Please push the finalized MAP + test artifacts to the Drive link and paste the HubSpot timeline. Procurement will review SLA-proposal.pdf and come back with minor redlines if any.

Let’s do the Wednesday walkthrough as suggested — 10:00am PT works. If you can share a calendar invite and the finalized MAP by end of day Tuesday, we’ll be ready.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Emily
